subject: Path analysis with correlation matrix as input  ("constrained estimation)

messages.author: 20a091f3d0e9ee8f
messages.subject: Path analysis with correlation matrix as input  ("constrained estimation)
parts:
Hi dear all,

I am trying to replicate a path analysis appeared in Kline (2nd ed., 2005, pp. 151, 179-180, pp 221-222), where he suggested to use a "constrained estimation" method. I did a normal fitting, but I do not the same results...can we do a constrained estimation  in lavaan?
My synthax below.

Thank you!!

lower<-'0.53
0.15 0.18
0.52 0.29 -0.05
0.30 0.34 0.24 0.09'

kline <- getCov(lower, diagonal = FALSE)
View(kline)
rownames(kline)<-colnames(kline)<-c("lmor",'illn','neuro','prel','dimses')


model1<-'lmor~dimses+neuro # Psychosomatic model
illn~lmor
prel~lmor'

fit1<-sem(model1, sample.cov = kline, sample.nobs=469)
summary(fit1, fit.measures=T, standardized=T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Path analysis with correlation matrix as input ("constrained estimation)
parts:
Kline suggested to use a "constrained estimation" method

What does that mean?  For valid SEs, I expect it means that the residual variances should not be free parameters, but should be constrained to 1 minus the explained variance (to guarantee that all variances = 1, which is true by design when analyzing correlations).
can we do a constrained estimation  in lavaan?

You would have to label the slopes and calculate explained variance within the model syntax, in order to constrain the residual variances to 1 minus explained variance.
